data.title: AEON Credit Service Systems Breached; Affected Customers' Cardless Payment Limits Set to Zero by Default
data.description:
AEON Credit Service (Asia) said it experienced a cybersecurity incident on November 18, and unauthorized third parties may have accessed its systems. The company notified the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data and the police, and appointed independent cybersecurity experts to investigate. It stressed that there is currently no evidence of improper use of data.

AEON set the transaction limits for affected customers' "cardless payment" services to HKD0 by default, and will reissue virtual and/or physical credit cards with new card numbers free of charge. The company will contact affected cardholders individually in the near term.

It said customers' credit limits, outstanding balances, repayment arrangements and reward points will not be affected, and reminded customers to update their card numbers with merchants authorized for autopay or direct debit after card replacement is completed.

data.title: Dollar set for flat week as haven bids counter yields
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar set for modest weekly drop, uncertain about stock outlook
  • Risk-sensitive currencies rise with US stock futures
  • Dollar garners support from higher US yields, safe-haven demand

By Stefano Rebaudo

The dollar was heading towards ending the week roughly unchanged as investors weighed the possible drag from lower US Treasury yields against rising safe-haven demand.

Concerns about a deeper fall in the stock market would strengthen expectations of a more dovish Federal Reserve, eroding the dollar's yield advantage.

Conversely, the same bout of risk aversion would boost demand for safe-haven assets, including the dollar, offsetting some of the pressure from lower yields.

"We expect the Fed to remain hawkish and the US economy resilient, and our multi-asset strategists remain upbeat on US equities and the AI theme," said Daragh Maher, senior forex strategist at HSBC.

"The main risk to our view is that renewed market weakness could erode rate support, with no guarantee that safe-haven demand would again compensate," he said, adding that December’s Fed rate forecasts would be pivotal to the bullish cyclical greenback story.

The dollar index started its rally in early November and hit a 22-month high of 104.53 earlier this week. It was last little changed at 103.76 and was on track for a weekly rise of about 0.02%.

US stock futures surged on Friday as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday with renewed appetite for beaten-down shares, following a seesawing of AI stocks this week as investors weighed more attractive valuations against persistent concerns about heavy spending on the technology.

"The high-beta Australian dollar, Kiwi dollar and Norwegian krone are leading gains in G10, although the moves remain modest compared with their recent losses," Francesco Pesole, forex strategist at ING, said.

"That suggests the forward-looking forex market remains cautious about calling an all-clear on risk sentiment," he added.

A so-called high-beta currency tends to amplify shifts in global sentiment, outperforming when risk appetite improves and underperforming when it fades.

The Norwegian crown rose 0.67% to 9.70 versus the greenback.

The Aussie dollar added 0.58% to $0.667, finding its feet after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

The New Zealand dollar was also supported by results of the general election, which reduced political uncertainty, even with no clear winner.

New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will seek the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to keep his ruling centre-right coalition in power after official results showed he fell just short of a parliamentary majority.

Geopolitics remained in the background but oil prices were on track to snap a three-week losing streak following attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure.

Higher Brent crude futures often underpin the dollar against the euro and yen, as they boost revenues for US energy exporters while increasing import costs for the euro zone and Japan.

The euro was roughly unchanged at $1.0971 with investors showing little reaction to news that Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos was set to be nominated as the head of the European Central Bank.

DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS

The US currency was steady at 159.27 yen amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention.

Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month.

"Broad dollar strength and relative rates favour yen weakness, but the threat of forex intervention limits the yen’s downside, without making 160 an official ceiling," HSBC's Maher argued.

"We expect the dollar/yen to trade within 156-160, mostly towards the upper end."

data.title: Gold gains nearly 3% as dollar rally stalls, equities stabilise
data.description:
Key points:
  • Don't see gold easily back to $5,000/oz, analyst says
  • Shares bounce after bruising month
  • Spot silver up over 6%

By Ashitha Shivaprasad

Gold prices rose nearly 3% on Friday, recovering from a more than one-year low, supported by a pause in the dollar's advance and calmer equity markets.

Spot gold rose 2.9% to $3,670.69 per ounce by 0835 GMT, after it touched its lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 3.9% to $3,669.30.

"After days of declines, buyers returned to the market. Technology and AI stocks seem to have stabilised after the recent selloff, which is positive for gold because the market rout had forced some investors to liquidate bullion positions to raise cash and cover losses in other positions," said Carlo Alberto De Casa, external analyst for Swissquote.

"I don't see gold easily back to $5,000, but I see good chances that the price could return to $4,000-$4,200."

The US dollar took a breather after scaling a 22-month peak earlier this week. A softer dollar makes dollar-priced metals less expensive for holders of other currencies.

Equities steadied as they neared the end of a bruising month, with a US holiday lull giving some respite from AI jitters.

The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation accelerated in October, data showed on Wednesday. These reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise rates next month and again in early 2027. (FEDWATCH)

Rising interest rates diminish gold's appeal by boosting returns on competing interest-bearing assets.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in key Asian hubs improved this week, with jewellery and investment buying picking up in India, while strong retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

Spot silver climbed 6.6% to $44.25 per ounce, platinum gained 5.4% to $1,360.82 and palladium rose 4.6% to $913.07. All three metals were on track for weekly gains.

data.title: Lumito enters into collaboration with CTC, strengthening its pathway to new customer projects in clinical research and drug development
data.description:
Lumito AB (publ) (“Lumito” or the “Company”) has entered into a collaboration with CTC Clinical Trial Consultants AB (“CTC”), a CRO company specialising in clinical research and drug development. Through this collaboration, CTC will be able to offer Lumito’s SCIZYS® technology in relevant customer discussions and studies where sensitive and quantitative analysis of tissue samples can create value. A concrete customer dialogue is already underway with one of CTC’s customers, together with Offspring Biosciences Sweden AB (“Offspring Biosciences”). For Lumito, the collaboration provides a new route to reaching a broader range of potential customer projects in clinical research and drug development.

During the development of new drugs, tissue samples can provide valuable information about how patients respond to treatment. SCIZYS® enables sensitive and quantitative analysis of specific biomarkers in tissue, including at low levels that are difficult to detect using conventional methods. This can provide important information for monitoring treatment response. For customers, this means access to a more detailed and reliable basis for decision-making when seeking to understand disease mechanisms, identify relevant biomarkers and evaluate the effects of different treatments.

CTC is a leading Clinical Research Organisation (CRO) in the life science industry. The company works closely with pharmaceutical developers and is well positioned to identify projects where this type of tissue analysis is relevant. By incorporating SCIZYS® into CTC’s offering, Lumito gains access to a broader range of customer discussions, while potential customers can assess the technology’s benefits in relation to their own research questions. The collaboration strengthens the link between SCIZYS® technology and concrete customer needs.

Together with Lumito’s existing partner Offspring Biosciences, the parties can combine CTC’s clinical trial services with Offspring Biosciences’ specialist expertise in tissue analysis and SCIZYS® technology. This provides customers with an integrated workflow, from biopsy and sample handling to biomarker analysis and reporting, without requiring them to coordinate all the specialist functions themselves. This model is already being applied in an ongoing customer dialogue, in which Lumito acts as a subcontractor to Offspring Biosciences.

“The commercial value of SCIZYS® is realised when our analytical capabilities meet a specific need among drug developers. Through CTC, we can get closer to these needs, and together with Offspring Biosciences, we can contribute to an integrated workflow from sample to analytical report. The fact that this model is already being considered in a customer dialogue represents an important step towards translating the technology’s potential into more customer projects” says Sanna Wallenborg, CEO of Lumito.

“We see a growing need for integrated solutions that combine clinical execution expertise with specialised analysis of biological samples. Through our collaboration with Lumito and Offspring Biosciences, we can complement our own expertise and offer our customers access to highly sensitive tissue analysis within relevant clinical development projects” says Johanna Flygt, Sales Director at CTC.

The collaboration between Lumito and CTC originated following an initial meeting at Venture Road UK in June 2026.

About CTC

CTC is a full-service CRO company offering consultancy, planning, execution and reporting of clinical studies. The company has particular expertise in early clinical development and provides a broad range of services, including project management, clinical monitoring, medical writing, biometrics and clinical pharmacology. Through its own research clinics in Sweden and the Netherlands, CTC supports drug development and clinical research across several phases. Founded in 2011, the company works with both smaller innovative companies and international pharmaceutical companies. www.ctc-ab.se

About Offspring BiosciencesOffspring Biosciences is a specialized contract research organization (CRO) focused on cell- and tissue-based research and development. The company provides advanced analytical services to the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, including target validation, antibody characterization and translational research in human tissue. www.offspringbiosciences.se

About Lumito

Lumito develops and markets innovative technology that opens up new possibilities for advanced analysis of tissue samples in research, drug development and digital pathology.

The Company’s patented SCIZYS® platform is based on upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) and combines very high detection sensitivity with minimal background interference. The technology enables the identification and quantitative analysis of specific proteins in tissue, even at low levels that may be difficult to detect using conventional methods. High signal stability and low background provide the basis for more detailed and reproducible tissue analysis.

SCIZYS® has the potential to support a shift from predominantly visual and semi-quantitative biomarker assessment to more sensitive, objective and quantitative analysis. This can provide researchers with new tools to understand disease mechanisms, identify biomarkers and develop more personalised treatment strategies.

Lumito’s vision extends beyond current research applications. By providing more detailed information about biological processes, the Company aims to contribute to the development of precision medicine, in which better medicines, diagnostics and more informed treatment decisions may, over time, lead to improved patient outcomes and more efficient use of healthcare resources.

For more information, please contact:

Sanna Wallenborg, CEO

data.title: Euro zone consumers sharply increase inflation expectation, ECB survey shows
data.description:
Euro zone consumers sharply raised their expectation for inflation in the year ahead last month and perceptions also rose significantly, a European Central Bank survey showed on Friday, bolstering the case for another interest rate hike.

Contemplating further policy tightening, the ECB has been monitoring consumer expectations closely, worried that energy price surges could set off hard-to-break second-round effects if households start demanding higher wages.

While these second-round effects have yet to become visible in the data, policymakers have been making the case for preemptive rate hikes, and the bank has all but promised another move, its third this year, on December 17.

Consumers surveyed by the ECB now see inflation at 3.5% in the year ahead, up from 3.1% the previous month, the ECB's October Consumer Expectations Survey showed.

The jump came as perceived inflation over the previous year surged to 4.1% from 3.6%, putting perceptions in line with the 4.0% consumer price change measured by EU statistics agency Eurostat, twice the ECB’s 2% target.

Expectations for three years ahead meanwhile rose to 3% from 2.9% and expectations five years ahead remained unchanged at 2.5%, the ECB said, based on a survey of 19,000 adults from 11 euro zone members.

Consumers, however, did not expect to recoup these real income losses, as they expected nominal incomes to increase just 0.6% in the year ahead, down from 1.1% seen in September.

The drop in earnings expectations was most pronounced in the lowest income quintile, the ECB added.

data.title: German unemployment rises more than expected in November
data.description:
The number of people out of work in Germany rose more than expected on a seasonally adjusted basis in November, labour office figures showed on Friday.

In seasonally adjusted terms, the jobless figure rose by 9,000 to 3.025 million, while analysts polled by Reuters had predicted an increase of 4,000.

The seasonally adjusted jobless rate remained stable at 6.4% from October.

Unadjusted, the total fell by 19,000 to 2.936 million, from 2.955 million in October. The labour office said the decline reflected the end of the autumn seasonal pickup. The unadjusted total has been below the 3 million mark since September.

Daniel Terzenbach, a member of the Regional Management Board of the Federal Employment Agency, said in a statement: "The slight economic recovery has not led to a revival in the labour market in November." He said the trends of recent months were continuing.

In total, 646,000 job openings were registered with the labour office in November, 23,000 more than a year ago.

data.title: Biocon gets Brazilian regulator nod for biosimilar Pertuzumab for breast cancer treatment
data.description:
Biocon Ltd on Friday said Hertuzo, a biosimilar Pertuzumab licensed to its partner Bionovis, has received approval from Brazilian regulator ANVISA for treating HER2-positive breast cancer.

The approval builds on Biocon's 10-year productive development partnership (PDP) in Brazil through a consortium with Bionovis and public pharmaceutical laboratory Bahiafarma, the company said in a statement.

Through the PDP, the consortium has an opportunity to supply locally manufactured biosimilar Pertuzumab to Brazil's public healthcare market, potentially broadening access and delivering savings to the healthcare system, the Bengaluru-based company said.

The nod follows recent approvals for Biocon's biosimilar Pertuzumab from the US Food and Drug Administration and the European Commission.

Susheel Umesh, Chief Commercial Officer for Emerging Markets and Head of Global API & Global BD at Biocon, said the ANVISA approval underscores the company's scientific and regulatory capabilities and the growing strength of its global oncology portfolio.

It enables the company to advance its PDP partnership with Bionovis and Bahiafarma, expanding access at scale to an affordable, high-quality biologic therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer patients in Brazil, he added.

data.title: Sensex falls 764 points, Nifty slips below 25,700 as IT, financials drag
data.description:
Benchmark indices traded sharply lower in afternoon trade on Friday as information technology and financial stocks declined, while the broader market held up better.

At 1.16 pm, the Sensex was at 83,564.55, down 764.04 points or 0.91 per cent from its previous close of 84,328.59. The index had opened at 84,093.24. The Nifty was at 25,673.60, down 210.90 points or 0.81 per cent from its previous close of 25,884.50. It had opened at 25,839.25.

Among Nifty 50 gainers, Bharat Electronics rose 1.85 per cent to ₹412. Titan gained 1.47 per cent to ₹4,699, JSW Steel added 0.94 per cent to ₹1,315.20, Trent rose 0.75 per cent to ₹3,287 and Hindustan Unilever gained 0.56 per cent to ₹2,142.70.

Shriram Finance led the losers, falling 3.73 per cent to ₹926. Bajaj Auto declined 2.80 per cent to ₹10,546, HCLTech fell 2.19 per cent to ₹1,436.40, Infosys lost 2.13 per cent to ₹1,157.80 and Bharti Airtel slipped 1.88 per cent to ₹2,063.

Among sectoral indices, Nifty IT was the worst performer, according to SBI Securities, as investors booked profits after Thursday’s sharp rally. Nifty India Defence was the best performer. On the BSE, 2,414 stocks advanced and 1,781 declined, while 257 were unchanged. The Nifty Midcap 100 rose 0.60 per cent and the Smallcap 100 gained 0.95 per cent. Within the Nifty, 15 stocks advanced and 35 declined.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said the market’s mood reflected pressure on several fronts. “The cautious tone reflects a combination of rising crude prices, a weaker rupee and lingering uncertainty over the India-US trade negotiations,” he said. He added that export-oriented sectors, particularly IT, remain vulnerable to the outlook for bilateral trade.

The rupee was trading around 92.56 to the dollar, weaker by about 0.1 per cent. Brent crude settled 2.07 per cent higher at $96.57 a barrel on Thursday, its highest since November 6, after reports of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and an attack on a Saudi refinery. Brent is still nearly 20 per cent lower for November. WTI crude was near $85.75. For India, a major energy importer, higher oil prices can raise the import bill and add to inflation concerns. OPEC+ is expected to keep production targets unchanged through March 2027 ahead of its meeting on Sunday.

On the BSE, 86 stocks hit 52-week highs and 107 hit lows. In all, 147 stocks were locked in the upper circuit and 176 in the lower circuit.

On the charts, SBI Securities placed Nifty support at 25,550-25,570 and resistance at 25,860-25,880. A fall below 25,550 could take the index to 25,380-25,400, it said. For the Sensex, it placed support at 83,300 and resistance at 84,200. In the options market, SBI Securities noted “meaningful call writing witnessed across 25800 & 25900 strikes,” while the 25,700 put strike has substantial open interest.

Commodities moved higher. MCX gold futures were near ₹1,24,140 per 10 grams, up about 1.5 per cent, and MCX silver was near ₹1,51,380 per kg, up about 3.8 per cent. MCX crude oil was near ₹7,960, up about 1.1 per cent. Gold was recovering from a 15-month low hit earlier this week. Enrich Money said a softer US dollar and a rebound in technology stocks supported prices, though expectations of further US Federal Reserve rate increases remain a headwind.

Bank Nifty opened near 63,326 and was holding above the 63,000-63,200 support zone, according to Enrich Money.

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus.com, advised investors in precious metals to “avoid chasing sharp daily rallies” and to consider staggered accumulation and sensible position sizing.

data.title: French Inflation Slides on Drop in Fuel Prices — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Ed Frankl

Inflation in France fell more than expected in November as fuel prices declined, but remained too high for the European Central Bank, which next month is expected to raise its key interest rate for a third time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran.

Consumer prices in the eurozone's second-largest economy were 3.2% higher than in the same month of 2025, a lower annual rate of inflation than the 3.7% recorded in October, France's statistics office said Friday. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a 3.6% rate of inflation.

Inflation in France climbed to its highest level in nearly three years in October, from an annual rate of just 1.1% in February, before the first U.S. airstrikes on Iran.

Oil prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a lasting resolution to the conflict, although they remain above prewar levels. As a result, prices of gasoline and other fuels have declined.

However, European natural gas prices remain near multiyear highs, which will keep household energy prices elevated throughout the colder winter months.

The ECB has raised its key rate twice so far this year, judging that the surge in energy prices was too great to ignore. Investors are primed for another hike before the end of the year.

The EU said last week that it expects French inflation to peak at 4.3% in the first quarter of 2027 due to further increases in energy prices and how they pass through into food and services.

Yet incoming data shows few signs of those energy costs spilling over into other parts of the economy. Services inflation, for instance, fell in November due to a sharp decrease in prices for accommodation and transport services.

It comes as France's economy appears to have been hit harder by the war than its neighbors. Gross domestic product sank 0.2% in the third quarter, dented by a drop in exports and lower private investment.

Investors have grown more concerned in recent months over the country's public finances, which sent government bond yields rising. Those higher bond yields, while ratcheting up nervousness around the economy, could help the ECB as they tighten monetary conditions before the central bank needs to raise rates.

French consumer spending was flat on month in October, data also published Friday showed, coming in the month when consumer confidence hit its lowest level in more than three years. While surveys of purchasing managers showed steady economic growth in Germany, there was a deepening downturn in activity in France.

In neighboring Spain, inflation also declined notably in November, falling to 4.1% from 4.9% in October, data published Friday showed.

Write to Ed Frankl at edward.frankl@wsj.com

data.title: Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools
data.description:
(08:33 GMT) *Meituan 3Q Rev CNY115.55B Vs. CNY95.06B >3690.HK
(08:34 GMT) *Meituan 3Q Net CNY2.07B Vs. Loss CNY18.63B >3690.HK
(08:49 GMT) Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools

By Tracy Qu

Meituan's profit was largely stable sequentially amid higher revenue in the third quarter as China's top food-delivery company continued to recover from a brutal price war.

The Beijing-based company on Friday said net profit was 2.07 billion yuan, equivalent to $310.7 million, for the three months ended September. It recorded a 2.15 billion yuan net profit in the second quarter and net loss of 18.63 billion yuan a year ago.

Revenue climbed 22% from a year earlier to 115.55 billion yuan.

The results beat market expectations. Analysts had expected net profit of 354.7 million yuan on revenue of 113.56 billion yuan, according to a FactSet-compiled consensus.

Meituan has been locked in a food-delivery price war since last year as Alibaba Group and JD.com pushed to gain more market share. Competition has normalized in recent quarters.

data.title: Euro zone bond yields rise with oil after choppy week for shares
data.description:
Euro zone yields rose on Friday, as investors returned to equity markets and oil prices were set to snap a three-week losing streak.

After a choppy week for shares, which sent many market participants in search of safe-haven assets, Germany's 10-year bond yield (DE10YT=RR), the benchmark for the euro zone, rose 1.8 basis points (bps) to 3.284%.

As a more risk-on environment returned, yields were also supported by Thursday's publication of minutes from the European Central Bank's October meeting, which showed that some policymakers were leaning towards an interest rate hike but opted for a delay to collect more evidence on inflation risks.

Money markets price in two ECB rate increases of 25 bps by June 2027, LSEG data showed.

Brent crude oil futures were up 1.2% as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil supply from the conflict-hit Middle East.

The 2-year German Schatz yield was steady at 3.076%. (DE2YT=RR)

Other euro zone yields were mixed. France's 10-year yield seesawed and was last down 1.6 bps at 4.727% while Italy's was little changed at 4.339%. , (FR10YT=RR)

Euro zone yields were still set for a weekly drop.

data.title: Lumibird Shares Surge After Thales Targets Majority Stake in $483 Million Laser Deal
data.description:
By Adam Whittaker

Shares in laser-technology company Lumibird soared after Thales said it was in exclusive talks to buy a majority stake that would value its photonics division at around 440 million euros, including debt, equivalent to $482.6 million.

In opening European trade, shares were 18.5% higher at 29.1 euros, lifting their year-to-date gains to 37%.

Aerospace-and-defense group Thales said Friday that it planned to buy a 51.6% stake in Lumibird from its chief executive officer and majority shareholder, Marc Le Flohic. Thales said the deal valued Lumibird at 30.10 euros a share. Lumibird shares closed Thursday at 24.55 euros. Thales expects to close the deal in the second quarter of next year.

The price per share paid could rise to 32.66 euros, depending on the completion of the sale of Lumibird's medical division.

Thales said the deal would create a European photonics platform and help it develop laser-directed energy weapons.

The company will later file a tender offer for all Lumibird shares that it doesn't hold and expects to complete this in the second half of 2027, it said.

Write to Adam Whittaker at adam.whittaker@wsj.com

data.title: Rheinmetall Gets $810 Million Tank Order From Romania
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Rheinmetall said it received an order valued at 738 million euros ($809.5 million) to supply dozens of its Lynx tanks to Romania, a key growth market for the German defense contractor.

The company said Friday that Romania placed an additional order for 66 Lynx combat vehicles under a framework contract signed in May. The Romanian fleet will mainly consist of infantry-fighting vehicles, supplemented by armored mortar, command post and medical variant vehicles, Rheinmetall added.

Romania had already ordered an initial batch of 232 vehicles when the broader framework contract--covering 298 Lynx vehicles in total--was first awarded.

The company said it is investing several hundred million euros in Romania to fulfill the orders it received there.

Rheinmetall has benefited in recent years from a flurry of contracts as European governments stepped up defense spending, but procurement delays for some of them prompted the company to cut its annual guidance twice this year.

Write to Adria Calatayud at adria.calatayud@wsj.com
